ui.title: Java Roadmap
ui.intro: 4 phases, 56 steps. Click Details on any topic to open it, and mark what you have learned as done.

phases.title: Phase 1: Java Fundamentals
phases.goal: Build a strong foundation in Java.
phases.milestone: You can write basic Java programs on your own.
topics: What Java is, its features and uses
Java is an object-oriented, platform-independent language used for Android apps, banking systems, web backends and enterprise software. Its motto: write once, run anywhere.
The JDK has the tools to write and compile code, the JRE provides what is needed to run it, and the JVM executes the bytecode. Flow: .java, compiler, .class, JVM.
Every program starts at public static void main(String[] args). Print output with System.out.println(). Compile with javac Hello.java and run with java Hello.
A variable stores data in memory, e.g. int age = 20;. Use the final keyword to make a value constant.
Primitive: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char, boolean. Non-primitive: String, arrays and classes.
Implicit casting widens automatically (int to double). Explicit casting narrows manually, e.g. int x = (int) 9.7; and can lose data.
Arithmetic (+ - * / %), relational (== != > <), logical (&& || !), plus assignment and increment operators.
Import java.util.Scanner, create new Scanner(System.in), then read input with nextInt(), nextLine() and similar methods.
Run different code depending on a condition using if, else if and else. Also learn nested if and the ternary operator.
Compare one value against many cases. Remember to add break after each case and a default case.
Repeat code. Use for when the count is known, while when it depends on a condition, and do-while when the body must run at least once.
The best practice for nested loops: the outer loop controls rows and the inner loop controls columns.
Split code into reusable blocks. Parameters are inputs, return values are outputs, and overloading allows the same name with different parameters.
Combine everything: calculator, even/odd, prime check, factorial, Fibonacci, palindrome and sum of digits.

phases.title: Phase 2: Arrays & Strings
phases.goal: Work with collections of data and text.
phases.milestone: You can solve coding problems on arrays and strings.
topics: Store many values of the same type: int[] a = new int[5];. Indexes start at 0 and a.length gives the size.
A table of rows and columns: int[][] m = new int[3][3];. Used for matrices and grids.
Loop through arrays with for and for-each. Learn linear search and binary search (on sorted arrays).
Bubble, selection and insertion sort. Arrays.sort() exists, but learn the logic first.
Strings are immutable. Understand the string pool and the difference between == and .equals().
length(), charAt(), substring(), indexOf(), toUpperCase(), trim(), split(), replace(), equals(), compareTo().
Mutable strings for frequent changes. StringBuilder is faster, StringBuffer is thread-safe.
Practice: reverse, palindrome, anagram, max/min, duplicates, vowel count, second largest.

phases.title: Phase 3: Object-Oriented Programming (OOPs)
phases.milestone: You can build a small Java application using OOPs concepts.
topics: A class is a blueprint and an object is a real instance of it. Classes hold variables (data) and methods (behavior).
A special method that runs when an object is created. It has the class name and no return type. Types: default, parameterized, copy.
Refers to the current object. Commonly used when a parameter and a field share a name: this.name = name;
Keep data private and expose it through getters and setters. This protects data and gives you control.
A class can reuse another class using extends. Types: single, multilevel and hierarchical.
Access the parent class's fields, methods and constructor with super, super.method() and super().
Same method name in the same class with different parameters. This is compile-time polymorphism.
A child class redefines a parent method with the same signature. Use the @Override annotation.
One interface, many forms. Compile-time (overloading) and runtime (overriding), e.g. Animal a = new Dog();
Show only what is essential and hide the details. Achieved with abstract classes and interfaces.
Declared with abstract and cannot be instantiated. They can have abstract methods (no body) and normal methods.
Define a contract of methods that a class promises to implement. A class can implement many interfaces.
public (everywhere), private (same class), protected (package and subclasses), default (same package).
static belongs to the class, not objects. final prevents changing a variable, overriding a method or extending a class.
Organize classes into namespaces with package and import. java.util and java.io are built-in packages.
Build a small app such as a Library or Bank system using classes, inheritance, interfaces and encapsulation.

phases.title: Phase 4: Core Java Advanced
phases.milestone: You can build real applications with collections, files and multithreading.
topics: Handle runtime problems without crashing. Checked exceptions are verified at compile time, unchecked ones occur at runtime. Learn throw and throws.
Put risky code in try, handle errors in catch, and run cleanup code in finally. You can use multiple catch blocks.
Create your own exception, e.g. class AgeException extends Exception, to enforce business rules.
Object versions of primitives: Integer, Double, Character, Boolean. Learn autoboxing and unboxing.
Write type-safe code such as ArrayList<String>. Wrong types are caught at compile time.
Ready-made data structures. Hierarchy: Collection, then List, Set and Queue. Map is separate.
ArrayList is a fast-access dynamic array. LinkedList is good for frequent inserts and deletes.
Sets do not allow duplicates. HashSet is unordered and fast, TreeSet keeps elements sorted.
Store key-value pairs. HashMap is fast, TreeMap keeps keys sorted.
Go through collection elements one by one using hasNext(), next() and remove().
Sort custom objects. Comparable defines a default order inside the class, Comparator defines custom orders outside it.
Create, read and write files using File, FileReader, FileWriter, BufferedReader and Scanner.
Convert an object to bytes to save it, and read it back later. The class must implement Serializable.
Run tasks concurrently. Extend Thread or implement Runnable. Learn start(), run(), sleep() and join().
Prevent conflicts when threads share data using the synchronized keyword and locks. Understand race conditions.
Short anonymous functions like (a, b) -> a + b, used with functional interfaces.
Process collections with filter, map, sorted and collect, e.g. list.stream().filter(x -> x > 10).
Modern date handling with LocalDate, LocalTime, LocalDateTime, Period, Duration and DateTimeFormatter.
